name: Cow and Fields
description: Bessie is out grazing on the farm, which consists of $$$n$$$ fields connected by $$$m$$$ bidirectional roads. She is currently at field $$$1$$$, and will return to her home at field $$$n$$$ at the end of the day. The Cowfederation of Barns has ordered Farmer John to install one extra bidirectional road. The farm has $$$k$$$ special fields and he has decided to install the road between two different special fields. He may add the road between two special fields that already had a road directly connecting them. After the road is added, Bessie will return home on the shortest path from field $$$1$$$ to field $$$n$$$. Since Bessie needs more exercise, Farmer John must maximize the length of this shortest path. Help him!
input_specification: The first line contains integers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$n-1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, $$$2 \le k \le n$$$)  — the number of fields on the farm, the number of roads, and the number of special fields. The second line contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$)  — the special fields. All $$$a_i$$$ are distinct. The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$m$$$ lines contains integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$), representing a bidirectional road between fields $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. It is guaranteed that one can reach any field from every other field. It is also guaranteed that for any pair of fields there is at most one road connecting them.
output_specification: Output one integer, the maximum possible length of the shortest path from field $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$ after Farmer John installs one road optimally.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1307D — Cow and Fields [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
